goal: Resolve F-005 so an agent subprocess that ignores SIGTERM after timeout must settle within a bounded time and leave no child or descendant process behind.

analysis.problem: Agent._callOnce sends only SIGTERM at timeout and then waits for close or error, so a child that ignores SIGTERM can keep the caller pending; independent close, error, and timeout handlers also do not establish a single terminal owner.
analysis.proposedApproach: Introduce a dedicated ChildProcessSupervisor and AgentTimeoutError at the agent subprocess boundary so termination escalates from SIGTERM to SIGKILL, terminal events settle once, and cleanup is owned by one component.
analysis.validation: Automated unit and agent tests must reproduce a SIGTERM-ignoring child, an exit-adjacent timeout race, a spawn error, and a descendant-process case. The Agent.call regression suite must assert: provider command and substituted argument dispatch remain identical before supervisor ownership; resolved agent.timeout seconds still convert to the expected millisecond deadline and bound completion within deadline plus grace plus margin; zero-exit text is returned once; JSON parsing remains selected by profile; stdout and stderr callbacks receive their chunks; retry repeats a failed/empty invocation and returns the recovered response; stdin fallback returns the full prompt; logger start/end events and agent metrics are recorded once per call; prompt-cache hits retain their response and metric behavior; temporary schema files are removed after both success and failure; non-zero exit remains an Error rejection; and timeout is AgentTimeoutError after SIGKILL with no live direct child or descendant.

knownFacts: src/lib/agent.js currently arms one timeout that calls child.kill("SIGTERM") and clears it independently in close and error handlers.
The Issue declares F-005, src/lib/agent.js, tests/agent/, and tests/unit/lib/ as the must scope.
The prepared worktree does not contain .tmp/refactoring/report.md, so that temporary report cannot be direct test input.

The retained public surface is Agent.call: provider command invocation, successful text or parsed JSON result, non-zero/spawn error reporting, retry behavior, stdin fallback, callbacks, logger events, prompt cache metrics, agent.timeout configuration, and temporary schema-file cleanup.
decisionPoints: The implementation must define a bounded grace period and an observable timeout failure contract.
The supervisor must own terminal-event arbitration and resource cleanup.
The implementation must terminate child descendants as well as the direct child when timeout occurs.
The supervisor must own only timeout lifecycle and terminal cleanup; Agent must retain invocation construction, output parsing, retry, callback, logging, cache, and schema-file cleanup ownership.
resolvedByProjectRules: The repository must use Node.js built-ins only and represent meaningful runtime behavior with classes.
The Issue is one concern and must not be split into separate specifications.
Tests must demonstrate the failure before the fix and must not alter flow artifacts to force a pass.
deferredToSpec: Exact grace-period value and process-group implementation details are deferred to source and test analysis.
The spec must map each acceptance criterion to an automated test or reproduction command.
The spec must map each retained Agent.call behavior to the existing owner or to ChildProcessSupervisor and include behavior-level regression evidence.

in: must update the agent subprocess boundary in src/lib/agent.js
must add automated timeout, race, spawn-error, descendant, and success-path regression coverage
out: must not address unrelated audit findings
must not publish packages, change dist-tags, or release software

impactOnExisting: must retain Agent.call invocation construction, provider parsing, retry behavior, stdin fallback, callbacks, logger events, prompt cache metrics, and schema-file cleanup under Agent ownership; ChildProcessSupervisor owns only direct-child and descendant timeout termination, terminal settlement, listeners, and timers.

must retain agent.timeout as the caller-visible timeout configuration; the new supervisor consumes its resolved timeout and adds a bounded internal grace period without a new public configuration surface.
must retain success behavior: zero-exit text and JSON responses, callback delivery, metrics, and retries must be verified through the Agent.call path after lifecycle ownership moves.
must retain failure behavior: spawn errors and non-zero exits remain Agent.call rejections, while timeout exhaustion becomes AgentTimeoutError with bounded completion and no surviving processes.

qa.question: Is there any remaining product decision that must constrain bounded timeout recovery behavior beyond the stated acceptance criteria?
qa.answer: No. The published Issue body is the accepted intent, and the worker must proceed without routine questions; its acceptance criteria define the required bounded recovery behavior.
qa.evidence: User instruction: accept the published Issue body as intent and proceed without asking routine questions; Issue #411 Acceptance Criteria; existing code pattern in src/lib/agent.js.
qa.why: The recommendation is based on the existing code pattern in src/lib/agent.js and the Issue acceptance criteria, which explicitly resolve the product-level timeout outcome while leaving implementation details to the spec.
qa.considered: Asking for a separate timeout-policy decision was rejected because it would repeat the accepted Issue intent.
